templates.template: Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP
templates.name: Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP
templates.description: Monitors ONLY the PDM appliance itself via authenticated HTTPS GET requests to /nodes/localhost/status, /nodes/localhost/rrddata and /nodes/localhost/certificates/info (expiry of PDM's own certificate). No remotes, PVE/PBS hosts, guests or managed storage are queried or discovered. Zabbix 7.0+; local RRD requires PDM 1.1+. Set {$PDM.URL}, {$PDM.TOKEN.ID} and {$PDM.TOKEN.SECRET}; grant Auditor to both user and token on /system/status. TLS certificate verification (peer and host) is disabled by default so the self-signed certificate PDM ships with works out of the box. To enforce verification, set "SSL verify peer" and "SSL verify host" on both HTTP agent items after installing the PDM CA on the Zabbix server/proxy (or replacing the PDM certificate) and using a URL that matches it. Failures are classified: HIGH when the request fails (see items "Status HTTP code" and "Status request result"), WARNING when the API answers but the payload is incomplete. Not covered: pending updates. See accompanying Dutch setup guide.

items.name: PDM: Get local node status
items.description: GET only; localhost refers to the PDM host itself. Headers and body are both retrieved and any HTTP status is accepted, so the dependent "Local node status payload" item can tell 401/403/404/5xx apart from transport failures (DNS, TLS, timeout), which are replaced by the marker TRANSPORT-ERROR. No managed resources are queried.

items.name: PDM: Local node status payload
items.description: Parsed status response: the PDM JSON plus "http" (status code), or {"http":<code>,"error":"<reason>"} on failure. All status metrics hang off this item.

items.name: PDM: Status HTTP code
items.description: HTTP status of the status request. 200 = OK, 401 = bad token, 403 = missing Auditor ACL, 404 = wrong URL/version, 0 = no HTTP response (DNS, TLS verification, timeout, refused).

triggers.name: PDM: Status request failed (HTTP {ITEM.LASTVALUE1}, 0 = no response)
triggers.expression: last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.http.code)<>200 and count(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.http.code,{$PDM.FAIL.WINDOW},"eq",200)=0
triggers.description: The PDM status request has not returned HTTP 200 for the whole window. See item "PDM: Status request result" for the reason: 0 = DNS/TLS/timeout/refused (if TLS verification was enabled, also check the certificate chain on the Zabbix server or proxy), 401 = token ID/secret, 403 = Auditor ACL on /system/status for both user and token, 404 = URL/PDM version.

triggers.name: PDM: No status samples
triggers.expression: nodata(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.http.code,{$PDM.NODATA})=1
triggers.description: Zabbix received no result at all from the status item (item disabled, proxy down, or {$PDM.NODATA} shorter than {$PDM.INTERVAL}).

items.name: PDM: Status request result
items.description: OK, or the reason the status request failed. Only changes (plus a daily heartbeat) are stored.

items.name: PDM: Local status API usable
items.description: 1 = HTTP 200 and the core fields (cpu, uptime, memory, root fs) are valid. All metric triggers are gated on this item.

items.name: PDM: Status schema complete
items.description: 1 = every field this template reads is present: cpu, wait, uptime, cpuinfo.cpus/model, loadavg[3], current-kernel.release, memory.free, swap.free, root.avail. Stricter than "Local status API usable"; 0 usually means a PDM update changed the status schema.

triggers.name: PDM: Status payload incomplete or unexpected
triggers.expression: last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.http.code)=200 and max(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.schema.complete,{$PDM.FAIL.WINDOW})=0
triggers.description: The API answers but one or more fields this template reads are missing or invalid, so some items are being discarded. Compare the payload (Test on "PDM: Get local node status") with the item list; the template may need updating for this PDM version.

triggers.name: PDM: CPU utilization high
triggers.expression: min(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.cpu.util,5m)>{$PDM.CPU.WARN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

triggers.name: PDM: CPU IO wait high
triggers.expression: avg(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.cpu.iowait,10m)>{$PDM.IOWAIT.WARN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1
triggers.description: Average CPU IO wait over 10 minutes above {$PDM.IOWAIT.WARN}%. Usually slow or saturated storage under the PDM appliance.

triggers.name: PDM: Load average per CPU high
triggers.expression: avg(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.load.5,10m)/last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.cpu.count)>{$PDM.LOAD.WARN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1
triggers.description: 5-minute load average, averaged over 10 minutes and divided by the number of logical CPUs, above {$PDM.LOAD.WARN}.

triggers.name: PDM: Recently restarted
triggers.expression: last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.uptime)<{$PDM.UPTIME.MIN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

triggers.name: PDM: Kernel release changed
triggers.expression: change(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.kernel)=1
triggers.description: The running kernel release differs from the previous value (update + reboot). Close manually.

parameters: var d=JSON.parse(value).data, o=d && d.memory; if(!o || typeof o.total!=='number' || typeof o.used!=='number' || o.total<0 || o.used<0) throw 'Missing or invalid counters'; if(o.total===0) throw 'Invalid total'; return 100*o.used/o.total;

triggers.name: PDM: Memory usage high
triggers.expression: min(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.memory.pused,5m)>{$PDM.MEMORY.WARN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

parameters: var d=JSON.parse(value).data, o=d && d.swap; if(!o || typeof o.total!=='number' || typeof o.used!=='number' || o.total<0 || o.used<0) throw 'Missing or invalid counters'; if(o.total===0) return 0; return 100*o.used/o.total;

triggers.name: PDM: Swap usage high
triggers.expression: min(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.swap.pused,10m)>{$PDM.SWAP.WARN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

parameters: var d=JSON.parse(value).data, o=d && d.root; if(!o || typeof o.total!=='number' || typeof o.used!=='number' || o.total<0 || o.used<0) throw 'Missing or invalid counters'; if(o.total===0) throw 'Invalid total'; return 100*o.used/o.total;

triggers.name: PDM: Root filesystem usage warn
triggers.expression: min(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.root.pused,5m)>{$PDM.ROOT.WARN} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

dependencies.name: PDM: Root filesystem usage crit
dependencies.expression: min(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.root.pused,5m)>{$PDM.ROOT.CRIT} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

triggers.name: PDM: Root filesystem usage crit
triggers.expression: min(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.root.pused,5m)>{$PDM.ROOT.CRIT} and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

items.name: PDM: Get local node RRD
items.description: GET only; localhost refers to the PDM host itself. Headers and body are both retrieved and any HTTP status is accepted, so the dependent "Local node RRD latest values" item can tell 401/403/404/5xx apart from transport failures (DNS, TLS, timeout), which are replaced by the marker TRANSPORT-ERROR. No managed resources are queried.

items.name: PDM: Local node RRD latest values
items.description: Newest valid value per RRD field (non-null, non-negative, at most 10 minutes old), as {"http":..,"available":0|1,"data":{field:value}}. One script parses the RRD response for all RRD items.

items.name: PDM: Recent local RRD available

triggers.name: PDM: Local RRD unavailable or stale
triggers.expression: max(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.rrd.available,{$PDM.RRD.WINDOW})=0 and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1
triggers.description: No recent RRD data. See item "PDM: Local RRD request result" for the reason. Local RRD requires PDM 1.1+.

triggers.name: PDM: No local RRD samples
triggers.expression: nodata(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.rrd.available,{$PDM.RRD.NODATA})=1 and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1

items.description: 1 = at least one RRD field has a value at most 10 minutes old. Deliberately independent of individual field names, so a field that is absent on some layouts never raises an alert.

items.name: PDM: Local RRD request result
items.description: OK, or the reason the local RRD request returned no recent data.

items.name: PDM: Network inbound
items.description: Newest non-null RRD value of this field, at most 10 minutes old (see "PDM: Local node RRD latest values"). The API already provides a rate: do not apply change-per-second. A missing field is discarded, never converted to zero. PDM 1.1+; root disk I/O may be absent for unsupported storage layouts.

items.description: Newest non-null RRD value of this field, at most 10 minutes old (see "PDM: Local node RRD latest values"). The API already provides a rate: do not apply change-per-second. items.name: PDM: Get certificate info
items.description: GET only. Reads the certificate PDM serves on its API/web port (self-signed, custom or ACME); any valid token may read it. Transport failures are replaced by the marker TRANSPORT-ERROR.

items.name: PDM: Certificate info payload
items.description: Parsed certificate info: {"http":..,"notafter":..,"days":..,"subject":..,"issuer":..}, or {"http":<code>,"error":"<reason>"} on failure.

items.name: PDM: Certificate days left
items.description: Whole days until the certificate expires; negative once expired.

triggers.name: PDM: Certificate expires in less than {$PDM.CERT.EXPIRY.WARN} days
triggers.description: Renew the PDM certificate (ACME renews automatically 30 days before expiry; check the ACME task log if this persists).

dependencies.name: PDM: Certificate expires in less than {$PDM.CERT.EXPIRY.CRIT} days

triggers.name: PDM: Certificate expires in less than {$PDM.CERT.EXPIRY.CRIT} days
triggers.description: Browsers and API clients that verify TLS will reject PDM once the certificate expires.

triggers.name: PDM: Certificate info unavailable
triggers.expression: nodata(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.cert.days,{$PDM.CERT.NODATA})=1 and last(/Proxmox Datacenter Manager self by HTTP/pdm.api.available)=1
triggers.description: No certificate expiry date for {$PDM.CERT.NODATA} while the status API works. See item "PDM: Certificate request result".

items.name: PDM: Certificate issuer
items.description: Equal to the subject for the default self-signed certificate.

items.name: PDM: Certificate request result
items.description: OK, or the reason the certificate request failed. Only changes (plus a daily heartbeat) are stored.

macros.description: PDM base HTTPS URL, without a trailing slash or /api2/json. Use a certificate-matching DNS name if TLS verification is enabled.
PDM API token ID; both user and token need Auditor on /system/status.
PDM API token secret.
Poll interval for the status and RRD requests (RRD resolution is 1 minute).
Status request must fail (or the payload be incomplete) for this whole window before alerting.
Alert when no status result arrives for this long. Keep it above {$PDM.INTERVAL}.
Local RRD must be unavailable for this whole window before alerting.
Alert when no RRD result arrives for this long. Keep it above {$PDM.INTERVAL}.
Seconds of uptime below which "Recently restarted" is raised.
CPU utilization warning percent, sustained 5m.
Memory used/total warning percent, sustained 5m. This is API used memory, not Linux MemAvailable.
Swap used/total warning percent, sustained 10m; no swap yields 0%.
Root filesystem used/total warning percent, sustained 5m.
Root filesystem used/total critical percent, sustained 5m.
CPU IO wait warning percent, averaged over 10m.
5-minute load average divided by logical CPUs, averaged over 10m.
Poll interval for the certificate info request.
Alert when no certificate expiry date arrives for this long. Keep it above {$PDM.CERT.INTERVAL}.
Certificate expiry warning, in days.
Certificate expiry critical, in days.
